title: Using Classification Keys
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Using Classification Keys Worksheets (Minibeasts and Animals)
standard_code: Year 4: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Explore and use classification keys to help group, identify and name a variety of living things in their local and wider environment.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on using classification keys: follow a branching key to name minibeasts and animals, and choose good yes/no questions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Answer yes or no, step by step.
key_sub: Start at question 1 and follow the branches to one name.
body_html:
How to think about it

A branching key uses yes/no questions to name a living thing.

  • Start at question 1. Answer yes or no, then follow that branch.
  • Keep going until you reach one name.
  • Good questions ask about features you can see or count: legs, wings, a shell.
Example

Snail or slug: which question?

Only one has a shell

Answer: Does it have a shell?

Example

Spider: Does it have legs? Yes. More than six? Yes.

Follow both Yes branches

Answer: spider

Common mistakes

  • Following the wrong branch.
  • Using opinion questions.
  • Starting in the middle of the key.

faq.q: How do I use a classification key?
faq.a: Start at the first question, answer yes or no about the living thing, and follow that branch until you reach its name.

faq.q: What makes a good key question?
faq.a: A question with a clear yes or no answer about a feature you can see, such as 'Does it have wings?'
To identify living things quickly and correctly, even ones they have never seen before.

items.q: What do you do after answering a question in a key?

items.q: Which question could you use in a key to separate a snake from a bat?
